M1: The difference between pointwise and uniform convergence: uniform convergence demands the SUPREMUM of the error tend to zero with n.
To refute uniform convergence, try finding for each n a special point (allowed to depend on n) where the function value does not shrink.
M2: Move terms across the inequality and define an auxiliary function that should be everywhere nonnegative; prove instead that its minimum is zero.
Differentiate the auxiliary function twice: the sign of the second derivative tells you the monotonicity of the first, locating the minimum.
